neighbours.label: an animal's body part or organ used in its survival behaviour (claws to dig, air sacs to attract, ovipositors to lay)
fire: A mole uses its broad forepaws to push through loose soil.
The frog inflates a vocal sac on its throat to call for a mate.
Female sawflies use an ovipositor to cut slits in leaves.
A lizard can drop its tail to escape from a predator.
Bats use echolocation to catch insects at night.
The pelican stores fish in a large throat pouch.
Beavers use their flat tails to slap the water in alarm.
Snakes detect prey with heat-sensing pits on the face.
quiet: A mechanic uses his broad wrench to loosen the old bolts.
The singer warms up her throat before she goes on stage.
The women use a sharp knife to cut slits in the dough.
The zoo keeps its lizards in a warm room near the entrance.
Bats were on sale at the sports shop last night.
The fishermen store fish in a large cooler.
Beavers are on the new stamp from Canada.
The snakes in the film look completely fake.
